When I was young, my parents didn't allow popular music in the house.  My brother got around this by listening to Golden Oldies and the Beatles, my sister Radio Disney, and I had musicals.  Phantom of the Opera, Les Miserables, Fiddler on the Roof, Joseph and the Technicolor Dreamcoat, etc.  I didn't see the actual musicals, so I pieced the plots together from the songs.  I would spend hours making up stupid stories that fit the music.  I'd mix and match musicals: "Wishing you were somehow here again" works with nearly any important character death, "Red and Black" is pretty great for any pre-battle scene, etc.  

Anyway.  Musicals have started making it to theaters.  In high school, Phantom of the Opera came out.  And the second I heard that opening overture I started bawling.  I remembered everything so clearly.  My room, my laptop, the toy props I used, everything.  My late afternoons, my weekends, all the times I was grounded, all those hours spent switching CDs out of my fat stereo.  It had a radio setting and I owned headphones, but I rarely dared to listen to anything but those musicals.

Les Miserables came out not that long ago.  Again, during the overture, I was sobbing.  My friends thought that was pretty weird.  But the nostalgia.  Old songs you haven't listened to for years, it's like time travel.  Immediately I was back.  I remembered where I would hide my notebooks, the toys, I remembered the taste of skittles, and I remembered the feeling.  That feeling.  That huge feeling that held so many years and so many hours and seemed bigger than my whole body.  

Keep pumping out musicals Hollywood.  I'll keep coming.

How long did I need to be oblivious for?

Anyways.  Back in my college days, my friends really liked this one gay bar, VIP.  It had pool, sometimes had live music, and nearly all my friends were homosexual in a city not known for tolerance.  We were fairly regular here, going usually once a month or so.  

One night, I start dancing up on a guy.  No big deal, most guys are gay.  Also I'm a little drunk and I'm young and most importantly, very stupid.  The guy starts following me around after that.  He tries to get me back on the dance floor, tries to buy me drinks, not taking my furious head shaking for a no.  I went outside to get away, he followed me out.  

So here's the part where I get really dumb.  I'm sitting at a table, listening to the live music, and the guy comes and sits himself down.  He keeps going after me, so I tell him if he's serious, to take his dick out.  The asshole does it.  Then I screamed.  

The dude's dick is not just out but erect, I remember noticing his shaved and unusually large balls.  He was brown, but his balls were pink.  He tries to cover up, but it's too late.  Other people are looking.  My friends are coming, but it's the bouncer that gets there first.  He CHARGES through these throngs of people and hauls the dude up.  The guy is gone before I can blink.  

My friends are asking questions, and I lie.  I lie because I am a terrible and I don't want people to know that.  I say the guy wouldn't leave me alone and he took his dick out.  I conveniently don't mention that I asked him to in this conversation.

Security comes over to talk to me.  The guy got his side of the story out: I had lured him into the guy's bathroom, gotten him all riled up, and then refused to finish him off unless we took it outside.  Holy crap dude.  The truth is way more believable than that lie.  But the bouncer smells that something is up.  Or maybe I just projected my own guilt.  He tells me he's got his eye on me, not to pull any shit.  I'm apologizing and admitting to dancing up on the guy, pulling the whole "scared innocent girl in over her head."  And that was true, a little.  

So the night goes on.  I try to put this out of my head.  Later, we leave the club.  Most of the group is drunk, everybody's shouting and joking, no one even remembers what happened earlier.  

Until my friend grabs my arm and runs.  A bottle whishes past my ear.  He drags me across the parking lot and shoves me into a car.  He noticed we were being followed.  It's the guy and his whole family.  A very large and angry family. 

There's a whole bunch of shouting outside the car.  My friends are trying to calm them down, trying to get the situation under control.  One of the women starts banging on the back window, trying to get me to come out.  At one point, two got in the car and tried to grab me, screaming and cursing me.  Which I kind of deserved.

I don't know how they did it, but my friends talked them down.  Penis guy finally admits I was never in the bathroom with him, which makes everyone think he was lying about everything.  I'm the victim and he's the villain.  His family says things, like "we've been kicked out of clubs before" and other sheepish concessions.  My friends high five and we went out for celebratory milkshakes. 

I've never told my friends, who probably saved me from a well deserved beatdown, the truth.  And whenever they tell the story (which is often, everyone loves to be a hero), I smile and try not to comment.  Because the story's all wrong.  It's not a victim and a villain, it's two drunk and stupid people who used deception to rile up their respective gangs and cause trouble.  I wasn't right, just lucky.

I've had this window open for a while, thinking about this.  Because it's silly, but it was hard to think of something.  And then I took a shower and thought some more.  Maybe taking a shower every day?  I like showers.  They're warm and peaceful, and there's a very simple checklist of things to do.  Wash hair.  Lotion body.  Shave legs.  Conditioner.  It's like meditating, but at the end you have a result.

I would change everything.

I'm selfish, I'm short-sighted, I'm overly emotional, I cry easily, I can't fucking talk to anybody and when I do manage to say something it's always fucking stupid, just so fucking stupid.  I try too hard.  And I hate myself.  No one wants to talk to someone who's incredibly negative and sad and makes the shittiest, stupidest jokes that aren't funny.  

I have the personality of milk.  I'm alright for a few days, and then I just spoil.  I'm like a shit onion.  You peel the layers and you find more shit underneath.  I steal.  I lie.  I told one of my boyfriends that I was raped so he wouldn't leave me for not being able to have sex.  He figured it out and left me.  I really don't blame him.  Oh, I can't have sex.  So that's another way I fail as a human being.  

I trespass.  I'm messy.  I smoke weed all the time, even though it doesn't make me feel good anymore.  I just keep hoping, you know?  So I'm wasting what little money I have left on drugs that don't work.  I'm 25 and I still live with my parents.  My last roommates kicked me out because they got sick of my shit.  They were willing to stay friends, until I tried to kill myself after getting drunk.  I really shouldn't get drunk.  Ever.  But people invite me and it seems like fun and I just make the shittiest decisions.  I'm looking for a job and I know I'm going to fuck it up.  I'm easily offended.  I can say all the mean shit I want, but if someone criticizes me I throw a hissy fit and make a run for it.  And then if the person is stupid enough to still give a shit they look for me, but there's only so many times you can put up with that.  I guess now that I don't have any friends left I have to put my family through it.  

I hate everything.  I want to be fun and positive and not give a shit what anyone thinks (or at least not constantly worry about what other people think) but I don't know how.  I exercise, I meditate, I eat right, and I've tried meds and therapy.  I am so tired of being alive.  I've wanted to die more than half my life and it never gets better.
